title: A. Delegato: Locality-Aware Atomic Memory Operations on Chiplets
problem: Chiplet-based architectures impose high, non-uniform memory access latencies across chiplet boundaries, severely degrading the performance of atomic memory operations (AMOs) used for fine-grained synchronization; existing solutions (near AMOs and centralized AMOs) either cause expensive cache-line ping-pong across chiplets or introduce coherence misses and require ALUs at the directory.
motivation: Chiplet integration is now the primary scaling mechanism for large core-count processors, but the interposer latency (e.g., 50 ns NVLink in NVIDIA Grace) makes conventional AMO execution strategies significantly less efficient than in monolithic designs, harming parallel workload throughput.
method: For atomic operations (read-modify-write instructions used for synchronization) on distant data, Delegated AMOs execute the operation at the current data owner without moving data, while Migrating AMOs transfer ownership to the requester (useful if the requester will access it again). Six static policies (All-Central, All-Migrate, Present-Central, Pinned-Owner, Unowned-Central, Chiplet-Aware) determine which approach fits based on data location. Delegato improves this by tracking a one-bit reuse flag that the directory's Predictor Table uses to learn access patterns and adapt between three strategies (Pinned-Owner, Present-Central, Chiplet-Aware). Testing used gem5 23.1, AMBA 5 CHI protocol, 32 out-of-order cores across two 16-core chiplets, and HeteroGarnet.
key_novelty: Delegated and Migrating AMO coherence transactions that allow operations to execute at the cache-line owner without moving data, paired with Delegato—a one-bit reuse tracker that feeds access patterns to the directory's predictor to enable adaptive strategy selection.
contributions: Two new far AMO coherence transactions (Delegated and Migrating) implemented within AMBA 5 CHI without requiring an ALU at the directory for Migrating
Five static directory AMO policies and a Chiplet-Aware policy exploiting requester and owner chiplet location
Delegato: a reuse-tracing mechanism piggybacking on SnpAMO responses to build a directory-level AMO predictor
1.13x speedup over state-of-the-art DynAMO predictor and 1.07x over All-Centralized AMOs, evaluated on 20+ benchmarks in gem5

metrics.speedup: 1.07x over centralized AMOs; 1.13x over DynAMO (state-of-the-art AMO predictor)
metrics.area: atomic ALU extension: 2894 um2 at TSMC 7nm (0.11% of Neoverse V1 core tile)
metrics.other: Delegated AMOs reduce critical-path inter-chiplet messages from 4 to 2 in pathological cases

baselines: single-chiplet and dual-chiplet NVIDIA Grace CPU configurations
limitations: Delegate transactions currently limited to single-owner scenarios (multi-sharer case deferred); performance gains are modest (1.07x-1.13x geomean) reflecting the narrow optimization window for AMO-heavy workloads on this architecture.
primary_theme: locality-aware atomic memory operation execution on chiplet architectures
